# later-in-source primary rule and its frame points at the real

# and the operand order flipped.) The byte-level guard is the bag twin
# Clone-carried operands (#36 review): a bag reached through a

# operand meeting a parsed one keeps the driving operand primary
# regardless of position (the TS site-url equality gate on the
# later-in-source flip, mirrored as the clone mark in go/val.go).
# THE EXCERPT GUTTER (the frame's line-number column). Two spaces, then
# the number RIGHT-ALIGNED to the widest line number the frame shows,
# which is always the last one -- the value's row plus two. The two
# leading spaces are the `-->` header's own indent, which is what lines
# These rows exist because a FIXED three-wide field agreed with the
# canonical port only while every shown number had one digit: from row
# eight upward the two engines printed the same error with differently
# indented excerpts, and the caret moved with the gutter, so every
# document past nine lines framed differently in Go than in TypeScript.
# One row per width. A row can only pin the gutter it EXPECTS to see --
# the excerpt's colour reset sits between the gutter and the source
